notes: Customer: mid-size cloud contact-center platform, integrates with Zendesk + Confluence + internal SQL + S3 blob store for KB
Primary goal: replace brittle internal heuristics with RAG-based agent assist that returns citations and provenance; must be auditable

Key features they asked for: token-level cost breakdown, deterministic citations (cite source + passage), freshness controls, multi-source retrieval prioritization (recent first), explicit fallback behavior when KB confidence < threshold
Latency/throughput targets: <400ms p50 for agent suggestions, sustained 2k reqs/min during peak campaigns, burst to 5k reqs/min for short windows
Failure modes: spike behavior during release days causes current service to degrade; need graceful degradation and model fallbacks to cheaper variants without losing citation guarantees
Quote from Head of Automation: 'We need answers that point to the doc. If the agent can't validate, it's useless.' Emphasis on source links and snippet-level citations.

Security/compliance: must support SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS for stored embeddings, audit logs for every retrieval and model call; data residency requirement: US-only storage for PII-indexed KBs.
Preference: open-model workflow ok for vector search and LLM orchestration but want ability to pin to validated model variants in Dedicated for predictable latency/cost.

POC ask: integrate Redwood RAG connector with their Confluence space + Zendesk KB; evaluate citation accuracy (precision@1 for top-1 citation), token-cost delta vs baseline, and latency under synthetic spike load
Internal stakeholders: Head of Product (Eva Soto), Head of Reliability (Tom Brenner), Security Lead (Rachel Kim). AE & SE (Ava + Marcus) demoed initial flows 2026-02-18.
Notes: they already run embeddings pipeline nightly; want Redwood Optimize suggestions on quantization and batching to reduce cost for long ticket contexts.
